title: OpenTelemetry moves GenAI, provider-specific and MCP semantic conventions into a dedicated repository
summary: In June 2026 the OpenTelemetry project split its GenAI, provider-specific and MCP semantic conventions out of the main semantic-conventions repository so they can iterate and version independently. The GenAI conventions remain marked as Development stability and had no official release as of late August 2026.

title: OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions define invoke_agent, chat and execute_tool spans for agent runs
summary: The GenAI semantic conventions define a span tree for agent execution: a top-level invoke_agent span for a full run, child chat spans for each model call, and execute_tool spans for each tool invocation, carrying attributes such as gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.response.finish_reasons.

title: LLM observability vendors consolidating: Langfuse and Galileo acquired within one quarter
summary: A community blog post reports that ClickHouse acquired Langfuse in January 2026 and that Cisco announced intent to acquire Galileo in April 2026, arguing teams should instrument to the OpenTelemetry standard rather than to any single vendor. No primary filing or company announcement is linked.

title: Report claims 85% of organizations now use GenAI somewhere in their observability stack
summary: A vendor blog cites a 2026 industry observability report stating that 85% of organizations use some form of GenAI for observability and that 89% of OpenTelemetry production users rate it favourably. The underlying report is referenced but not linked, and the sample and methodology are not described.

title: OpenTelemetry ships GenAI semantic conventions v1.0 GA with stable agent-graph and guardrail spans
summary: A post announces that OpenTelemetry has declared the GenAI semantic conventions generally available at v1.0, freezing the gen_ai.* namespace and adding stable spans for agent graphs, guardrail decisions and human approval gates. No release tag, changelog entry or SIG announcement is linked.

title: AgentTrace Protocol 2.0 becomes mandatory for all MCP server implementations
summary: An anonymous post claims a specification called AgentTrace Protocol 2.0 is now a mandatory conformance requirement for every MCP server, and that non-conforming servers will be delisted from public registries. No specification document, governing body or repository is identified.

title: Breaking: OpenTelemetry forms a GenAI Special Interest Group to standardize LLM tracing
summary: A post presents the formation of the OpenTelemetry GenAI Special Interest Group under the Semantic Conventions SIG as a brand-new development. The SIG was in fact formed in April 2024 and its scope has since expanded well beyond LLM client call tracing.
